_S7b_prod_attribution.instrument_upgrade: NEW AND IMPORTANT (see finding F10). The prod ingest consumer Srs08P0Ha3Cv--YPx0-Yn runs an LLEN of sorento-respond-message as its FIRST node ('Redis1') on every 5s poll, and that value is retained in execution data. The consumer ledger is therefore a complete 5-second-resolution LLEN time series of the prod sink. This fully defeats the drain-blindness that finding F7 flagged last cycle — a write at time T that is drained by T+3s is still visible as a non-zero LLEN in the poll that consumed it, and the pop itself appears as a non-empty 'Redis' node output.

A raw execution count is therefore a clock, not a leak signal. The sound signal is the per-execution Redis1 LLEN value and the Redis pop payload. Recorded so the reviewer does not re-apply the counting method.
_S7b_prod_attribution.sampling_strategy: A leak from this harness can only land in the 5s poll window immediately following one of the three known write instants. Those three polls were fetched in full rather than sweeping ~140 executions.

F9_STEP7_does_not_close_G1.severity: MEDIUM — coverage claim in the diff is incorrect; NOT a safety issue
F9_STEP7_does_not_close_G1.detail: Diff STEP 7 claims: 'OBS-15/16 assertion 2 can now be asserted directly off a rendered outgoing blob at the TEST sink, closing G1', and predicts the per-case TEST-sink delta rises from 1 to 2. Both claims are FALSE. The ingress clones hardcode is_test = {{ true }} on the sendmsg caller. BLOBTEST's test-guard sends is_test===true to output 0, which connects ONLY to test-guard-record — a terminal node with no downstream. The save-blob path (If -> Code in JavaScript -> If1 -> Loop Over Items -> Send a Message -> save) is reachable only via the guard's FALSE arm. Repointing STANDIN -> BLOBTEST therefore changes nothing observable for a caller passing is_test=true: both forks stop at their respective guard record.
F9_STEP7_does_not_close_G1.empirical_proof: Sub-execution 9426540 (OBS-15) executed exactly 3 nodes — When Executed by Another Workflow, test-guard, test-guard-record — with lastNodeExecuted 'test-guard-record'. Sub-execution 9426739 (OBS-16) identical. TEST-sink delta for the whole cycle was +3, not the +5 that 2-rows-per-Hop-3-case would require.
F9_STEP7_does_not_close_G1.why_it_is_not_a_safety_problem: The behaviour is strictly SAFER, not less safe: the test guard fired and short-circuited exactly as designed. Nothing leaked. This is a coverage-fix that did not land, not a containment failure. S1-S8 all still pass.

This is the tester's recommendation — the residual risk is very low and the alternatives all cost containment clarity.
(b) Add a THIRD fork whose test-guard records the egress AND falls through to the blob path, and point the clones at that. Costs a new artifact to keep S8-clean.
(c) Make the ingress clones pass is_test=false. NOT RECOMMENDED — it removes a guard for a coverage nicety and makes the clone's containment depend on BLOBTEST's node-type purity alone.
In all cases: correct the STEP 7 text and the S7a expected-count in the diff before the reviewer signs off, so the record does not carry a false coverage claim.

F10_consumer_ledger_is_an_LLEN_time_seri.severity: PROCESS — harness improvement, supersedes part of F7 and corrects the prior cycle's S7b method
F10_consumer_ledger_is_an_LLEN_time_seri.detail: The prod ingest consumer Srs08P0Ha3Cv--YPx0-Yn runs `LLEN sorento-respond-message` as its FIRST node on every 5s poll and retains the value in execution data. The ledger is thus a complete 5s-resolution time series of the prod sink depth, plus a per-poll record of whether anything was popped (the 'Redis' node emits {"":null} on an empty pop). This is a genuinely drain-independent instrument and is the correct primary evidence for S7b.
F10_consumer_ledger_is_an_LLEN_time_seri.correction: The prior cycle recorded the S7b method as 'counting consumer executions started inside the run window'. That is unsound: the consumer emits one execution per poll unconditionally, so the count is a clock, not a leak signal (~140 executions in an 11-minute window this cycle). The count must not be used. Use the per-execution Redis1 LLEN value and the Redis pop payload.
